newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zaire's Kabila says hopes for peace talks soon.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Kabila says hopes for peace talks soon.

text.p: Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila said after talks with South African President Nelson Mandela on Wednesday that he hoped direct negotiations could begin soon on a peace deal to end Zaire's civil war.

Kabila said he came at Mandela's invitation to the president's Johannesburg home to brief him on the situation in eastern and southern Zaire. "We must assume that peace can be found with the regime of Mr (Zairean President) Mobutu (Sese Seko). Let's hope the negotiations will start soon," he said.

Asked if the two sides in the Zaire conflict were close to a ceasefire agreement, Kabila said: "We are not close to a ceasefire agreement, we are close to negotiations." He made clear he was ready for direct talks with the Mobutu government about a truce.

Mandela's aides earlier said no statements of any kind would be issued to the media following the meeting which lasted roughly an hour. However, the South African president introduced his guest to reporters and invited him to answer any questions.
"General Laurent Kabila came down here to brief me about the situation. We are discussing very sensitive matters where confidentiality is absolutely necessary," Mandela said.
Kabila, who arrived amid great secrecy in South Africa on Tuesday, said he was "very glad for the advice (Mandela) gave me".
